data.name: Exotic Matter
data.detailed_description:
Shipwrecked on an alien planet light years from earth, you are tasked with finding a rare and invaluable substance that could save humanity from complete destruction.

Explore the randomly generated open world of planet Xcylin, delve into the ruins left by an alien race, and expand your arsenal and abilities. Exotic Matter offers countless items, weapons and block types to discover and unlock on your adventure to save Earth.

Exotic Matter is a single-player open world voxel Metroidvania adventure, currently being developed for PC. A blend between a sci-fi mystery and a survival/crafting experience, Exotic Matter takes you on a compelling adventure through fully simulated planet with roguelike underground facilities. The game's sophisticated "dungeon" generation system ensures that no two playthroughs or dungeons are ever the same.

Exotic Matter also features a fully moddable engine, allowing you to explore countless other worlds created by the community or put on your creative hat and make your own sci-fi adventure!

Features
  • a completely simulated planet open for total exploration
  • fully destructible and reconstructible terrain
  • build your own shelters/bases with sophisticated in-game technology. Connect lights and doors with switches, pressure sensitive blocks and even in-game computer systems
  • mine resources deep below the surface and find hidden treasures and secret underground complexes
  • a vast amount of different block types, each with different attributes and abilities
  • tens of ancient items and technologies left behind by an alien civilization
  • a crafting system combining personal crafting and large-scale crafting via replicator technology, for even more complex items
  • tens of roguelike facilities for you to explore - some large and important, some small and secret - all created by a sophisticated dungeon generation system
  • a "wide linear", deep sci-fi narrative driven by your own exploration and sense of adventure
  • intelligently interacting and overlapping procedural generation systems - from the alien landscape to secret facilities - ensuring no two adventures ever play the same
  • a fully moddable engine allowing you to create your own entirely custom worlds. Built-in modding support means that almost every aspect of the game is laid open to your creativity (from items and block types to planet composition and terrain, to biomes, and more)!

Please note that although these features are all planned and most of them are fully implemented, they are all subject to change due to the fact that this is an Early Access game. We are working on a new roadmap to prepare Exotic Matter for full launch - we'd love to hear your feedback on the Exotic Matter Discord

data.short_description: A blend of Metroidvania adventure and procedural survival game, in Exotic Matter you will explore, craft, fight, solve puzzles and survive. As the sole survivor of a last-ditch expedition to an alien planet, your duty is to find a powerful alien material that could save Earth from destruction.

reviews.review:
I see what this game was trying to do and I really wanted to like it, but it just isn't very good at the moment.  Perhaps things will improve throughout early access, but as of right now this is not a great game.  It's very similar to Minecraft and other "block open-world" games, so expect familiar gameplay and look.  Navigating the menus is a chore, and it's either not clear how to do something, or they made it harder than it should be.  I wasn’t able to figure out how to use several important items in the game.  Neither left nor right clicking would “use” the item when equipped, and nothing in the menu seemed to work either.  This is certainly an area that I expect will improve over the course of early access.

I'd like to start with some positives before fully diving into the negative.  I liked the crafting system.  You find schematics and then put them into the replicator.  It'll tell you which and how much of each item or resource you need to complete the schematics.  Overall it's really easy to use, and makes it clear how to build things.  The game has a few good songs on its soundtrack, which is important for lonely games like this.  I also loved the game's skybox.  It's incredibly beautiful and I enjoyed watching the planets and stars move around in the sky throughout the course of the day and night cycle.

Now for the game's many cons.  When your character wakes up, it's not at all clear what you're supposed to do next.  The game states to look for the rest of the crew, so you'll explore the whole shop reading their entries in computers.  After not finding them on the ship, you need to explore the open world, and it's here that the game falters.  The world is incredibly boring.  Most blocks look the same, and it's hard to tell the difference between each type.  This is a problem because your starting laser can only destroy certain types of blocks.  It's mostly just a grey dull world, with the occasional interesting feature, such as odd shaped trees, the nice looking skybox, or the colorful water.  The game lacks any water physics, and thus it acts like a normal block with the exception that you sink to the bottom of water.  You can't swim, so getting out of water requires that you destroy the water blocks to get out.  Water blocks act like any other block when destroyed, and the lack of physics is very noticeable.  If you destroy the blocks around water, and it'll just remain intact rather than spilling out as it does in Minecraft and other similar games.  I'm talking about the water a lot here because there is very little else in the world to talk about, and this water covers the world, requiring that you either destroy it or go around it to explore.

We explored the surrounding area and found very little of interest.  We did find some small robots flying around, but there wasn't any way to interact with them.  They didn't even react to our attacks.  I'm sure you can find the dungeon facilities that are shown in the trailer somewhere in the world, but locating them will require that you explore a vast, dull land of sameness.  Finding those facilities may spice up the gameplay with some combat, something we never experienced.  But we explored for over an hour and never saw anything we didn’t see in the first 2-3 minutes outside of the ship.

I'm being quite harsh on this game, more than I'd like to.  Because I think this could be a fun game once they add a whole lot more to the open world, and polish up the gameplay.  But as of right now, this game is not worth buying, certainly not at its $20 price, unless you simply want to support the development of it.

Check out our video linked below if you want to see 41 minutes of gamplay.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vPA4O3HTC0E
reviews.developer_response:
Thank you Praetorian and Jynx for your detailed review. I'm sorry to hear that you struggled to grasp some basic concepts of the game right from the beginning. We’re looking into that now and will try to include means to help players better find their way into the game in one of the next updates.

After carefully watching your Let's Play I noticed that there was still a small but significant bug: you were able to break glass with the Emergency Drill. This should not have been possible, and I think that lead to the problem of you not finding the waypoint to the repeater station. Which would have been the next thing to explore and from there on you would have found more waypoints that would ultimately lead you to the first facility (the Observatory).

So again, thank you for testing our game and helping us to identify potential problems. We really appreciate that and hope you’ll come back to the game on a later point in time to check the progress :)

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 (64bit)
  • Processador: Intel Core i5 (or comparable AMD CPU)
  • Memória: 6 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Nvidia GTX 580Ti (or comparable AMD GPU)
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 4 GB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: Please note, that there is no 32bit version of Exotic Matter. So please make sure you have a 64bit OS.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Sistema Operativo: Windows 10 (64bit)
  • Processador: Intel Core i7 (or comparable AMD CPU)
  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: AMD Radeon RX 480 or better / NVidia GTX 1060 or better
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 10 GB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: Please note, that there is no 32bit version of Exotic Matter. So please make sure you have a 64bit OS.
